Regions can define their own destinations (custom OpenStreetMap tags or supplied datasets), pool categories, and configure additional combined-access sets and activity-centre definitions (a network location whose walkable catchment, default 400 m, contains at least one destination of every required category).  These follow the same naming patterns, e.g. all_<set>_<variant> for a named combined-access set and activity_centre_<definition>_<tier> for a named activity centre.  Combined-access composites have access indicators only (no nearest-distance variables).

Distance threshold (m).  Distances can be customised to locally policy-relevant values.  The core walking access indicators use the configured neighbourhood accessibility threshold (default 500 m).  Where a region configures the optional pedestrian accessibility analysis, walking access is additionally evaluated at each configured pedestrian distance, and cycling access at each configured cycling distance (defaults: 500 m, 1000 m, 2000 m and 5000 m), so an access variable exists for each distance.

Cycling route stress measure, appearing as an optional prefix on cycling variable names: "lts1_" for routes composed entirely of lowest-stress Level of Traffic Stress (LTS) 1 links (suitable for all ages and abilities); "safe_" for fully low-stress routes on LTS 1–2 links (the default headline measure); or no prefix for danger-weighted routing over the full cycling network (higher-stress links usable at a proportionate distance penalty).  Which measures are computed is configurable (cycling_indicators contrasts and measures settings).

Heat Exposure Index (HEI): the heat exposure sub-index, derived from land surface temperature
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Land surface temperature (°C): the temperature of the Earth’s surface, indicating the lived experience of heat (Landsat 8 surface reflectance, hottest third of the year)
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Heat Sensitivity Index (HSI): the equally weighted heat sensitivity sub-index of land surface albedo, NDVI, NDBI, local climate zone, population density and vulnerable population
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Land surface albedo: solar reflectance, where higher reflectance implies less surface heat retention (inverted, so that higher values indicate greater heat vulnerability)
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI): a spectral index of vegetation health and greenness (inverted, so that higher values indicate greater heat vulnerability)
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Normalised Difference Built-up Index (NDBI): a spectral index of impervious surfaces such as concrete and asphalt
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Local Climate Zone: a standardised classification of land cover typologies for urban heat island studies, ordered from least heat retaining (water) to most heat retaining (bare rock or paved)
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Population density (persons per km²), from the GHS-POP global human settlement population grid
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Vulnerable population (%): those most at risk from heat on the basis of age, being the combined proportion of the population aged 0–4 and 65+ years
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Adaptive Capability Index (ACI): the equally weighted adaptive capability sub-index of child dependency ratio, subnational Human Development Index and infant mortality rate; higher values indicate lower adaptive capability
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Child dependency ratio: children (aged 0–14 years) relative to the working age population (15–64 years), indicating economic reliance
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Subnational Human Development Index: human well-being assessed through education, health and standard of living
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Infant mortality rate: deaths of children under 1 year of age per 1000 live births, a key indicator of population health
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Global Urban Heat Vulnerability Index (GUHVI): the equally weighted composite of the Heat Exposure, Heat Sensitivity and Adaptive Capability indices, (HEI + HSI + ACI) / 3
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Global Urban Heat Vulnerability Index (GUHVI) class, from 1 (least vulnerable) to 5 (most vulnerable)
Scale: sample point, grid, city, custom areas

Indicator: Percentage of population in Global Urban Heat Vulnerability Index (GUHVI) class 5, the most vulnerable class
